claim: At 18hpf, prior to the emergence of the simple squamous epithelium of the roof plate, the hindbrain neural tube is a pseudostratified columnar epithelium that is indistinguishable from other regions of the central nervous system.
source: At 18hpf, prior to the emergence of the simple squamous epithelium of the roof plate, the hindbrain neural tube is a pseudostratified columnar epithelium that is indistinguishable from other regions of the central nervous system.
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data from the study describing the developmental state at 18hpf.

claim: Over 12 hours from 18hpf, the dorsal region of the ventricle expands greatly and the dorsal midline of the neural tube generates a squamous epithelium that roofs over the expanding fourth ventricle.
source: However, over the next 12 hr the dorsal region of the ventricle expands greatly and the dorsal midline of the neural tube, specifically within the hindbrain, generates a new tissue type comprising a squamous epithelium that roofs over the expanding fourth ventricle.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse confocal microscopy observations documented in the study.

claim: The roof plate widens precociously at rhombomeres 2, 4 and 6, while rhombomeres 3 and 5 lag behind.
source: Along with the ventricular cavity, the roof plate widens precociously at rhombomeres 2,4 and 6, while rhombomeres 3 and 5 lag a little behind, and gradually extends its caudal limit (the obex) to the level of somite 3/4.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing differential timing of roof plate widening across rhombomeres.

claim: The interface between squamous roof plate and columnar neuroepithelium may be composed of a single cell with a medial protrusion linking to the squamous cells.
source: Transverse confocal sections show a rather abrupt transitional zone interface with the adjacent columnar neuroepithelium at the rhombic lip (Figure 1B,D), and this is confirmed by electron microscopy that suggests the interface may be composed of a single cell with a medial protrusion linking to the squamous cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy data showing the cellular architecture at the transition zone.

claim: At 17 hpf, dorsal columnar epithelial cells have aligned themselves on either side of the neural midline to generate the nascent ventricular surface.
source: At 17 hpf these two populations can be identified before the squamous roof plate forms. Dorsal columnar epithelial cells have aligned themselves on either side of the neural midline to generate the nascent ventricular surface (Figure 2A bottom panel and Tawk et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data and a citation to previous work (Tawk et al., 2007).

claim: A layer of overlapping irregular cells spans the midline at 17 hpf, sandwiched between the columnar epithelium and the overlying enveloping layer.
source: Dorsal to this, a layer of overlapping irregular cells spans the midline, sandwiched between the columnar epithelium and the overlying enveloping layer (EVL) (Figure 2A top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing the cellular organization at the dorsal midline.

claim: Irregular dorsal cells express little and patchy Pard3-GFP, in contrast to the polarised expression in columnar neuroepithelial cells.
source: In contrast to the polarised expression of the apical protein Pard3-GFP within the apical end feet of the columnar neuroepithelial cells (Figure 2B bottom), the irregular dorsal cells express little and patchy Pard3-GFP (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data showing differential Pard3-GFP expression patterns.

claim: Irregular dorsal cells rearrange themselves so that there is no or very little overlap across the dorsal midline over a period of 40 minutes.
source: Over a period of 40 min, the irregular dorsal cells rearrange themselves so that there is no or very little overlap across the dorsal midline, thus forming a rectilinear interface at the dorsal midline (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data tracking cell rearrangement.

claim: As the ventricle begins to expand, the lateral membranes of some dorsal midline cells take on a distinctive spiky appearance.
source: Next, as the ventricle beneath them begins to expand the lateral membranes of some of these midline cells take on a very distinctive spiky appearance (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing morphological changes during ventricle expansion.

claim: Dorsal cells gradually lose spiky lateral protrusions and transform to a squamous, polygonal morphology over a period of 4 hours as the ventricle enlarges.
source: As the ventricle enlarges over a period of 4 hr some of the dorsal cells gradually lose the spiky lateral protrusions that were contacting the basolateral domains of the columnar epithelia and the cells transform to a squamous, polygonal morphology thus forming the first distinctive squamous roof plate architecture (Figure 2E; Figure 2—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data documenting the transformation process.

claim: In rare examples, irregularly shaped midline cells undergo pronounced rostrocaudal migrations before integrating into the expanding squamous roof plate.
source: In rare examples, irregularly shaped midline cells undergo pronounced rostrocaudal migrations before integrating into the expanding squamous roof plate (Figure 2F; Figure 1—video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing cell migration events.

claim: Differentiation into squamous roof plate is accompanied by transformation of irregular Pard3-GFP distribution into a continuous Pard3-GFP domain around the entire polygonal cell perimeter.
source: Differentiation into the squamous roof plate is accompanied by maturation of their Pard3-GFP expression patterns: the irregular distribution of Pard3-GFP in cells prior to their transition into squamous roof plate is transformed into a continuous Pard3-GFP domain around the entire polygonal cell perimeter when they are properly part of the squamous roof plate (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data tracking Pard3-GFP expression during differentiation.

claim: Columnar epithelial cells were never observed to transform into squamous cells.
source: In contrast to the irregular cells, the adjacent columnar epithelial cells were never observed to transform into squamous cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative observations from extensive time-lapse imaging.

claim: The squamous roof plate is pioneered by mesenchymal cells at the dorsal midline of the neural tube.
source: Our time-lapse analysis hence shows that the squamous roof plate is pioneered by mesenchymal cells at the dorsal midline of the neural tube.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from time-lapse imaging data showing the origin of squamous roof plate cells.

claim: Cells at the columnar-squamous interface have a characteristic irregular membranous extension that drapes over adjacent columnar rhombic lip cells.
source: These cells have a characteristic irregular membranous extension that drapes itself over the adjacent columnar rhombic lip cells and a cell body with nucleus that sits just medial to these columnar cells (i.e. just within the roof plate territory) (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing the morphology of cells at the interface.

claim: The interface between epithelial types is populated by a single distinct cell type termed a 'veil cell'.
source: These results show that the interface between epithelial types is populated by a single distinct cell type, which we term a 'veil cell' after its veil-like lateral membranous extension.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from morphological analysis of cells at the epithelial transition zone.

claim: The veil cell's membranous extension is in intimate contact with the underlying atoh1a-positive cells of the rhombic lip.
source: To define more precisely the relationship of veil cells to the columnar rhombic lip cells, we analysed veil cell morphology in the atoh1a:EGFP transgenic line that reveals rhombic lip cells. This shows that the veil cell's membranous extension is in intimate contact with the underlying atoh1a-positive cells of the rhombic lip (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data from transgenic reporter lines showing spatial relationships.

claim: Pard3-GFP is excluded from the veil and forms a ring that outlines the apical end foot of veil cells.
source: Using Pard3-GFP expression to define the apical surface of veil cells, we find Pard3-GFP is excluded from the veil and forms a Pard3-GFP ring that outlines the apical end foot of the veil cells that connects both medially to the large interface with squamous cells of the roof plate and laterally to the mosaic of small apical end feet of the columnar epithelium of the rhombic lip (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence imaging data showing Pard3-GFP localization in veil cells.

claim: The apical surface of each veil cell has a cilium that is close to their nucleus and protrudes into the ventricle.
source: The apical surface of each veil cell has a cilium that is close to their nucleus and protrudes into the ventricle (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing cilium localization in veil cells.

claim: Within the veil, microtubules are distinctly polarized and organized into near linear arrays.
source: Within the veil, microtubules are distinctly polarized and organized into near linear arrays of microtubules (Figure 3F), in contrast to the radially organized microtubule cytoskeleton of cells lying fully within the squamous roof plate (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data showing microtubule organization in veil cells.

claim: The lateral veil of veil cell progenitors is highly motile and constantly remodels its borders.
source: This revealed the lateral veil of these progenitors (that overlies the neuroepithelial rhombic lip cells) is highly motile and constantly remodels its borders.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse microscopy data showing dynamic veil behavior.

claim: The mean length of the veil is 27 μm ± 2.8 (n = 20).
source: The mean length of the veil is 27 μm ± 2.8 (n = 20) and thus covers approximately 60% of the basolateral surface of the underlying columnar rhombic lip progenitors, which are 45 μm ± 3.2 long (n = 20).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements from imaging data.

claim: Veil cells collectively form a continuous population at the interface of columnar and squamous tissues that maintains consistent contact with atoh1-positive cells of the rhombic lip.
source: Despite the highly dynamic nature of individual veils, veil cells collectively form a continuous population at the interface of columnar and squamous tissues that maintains a consistent, if constantly adjusted contact with atoh1-positie cells of the rhombic lip (veils of adjacent cells are highlighted in Figure 4A; Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing collective veil cell behavior.

claim: Veil cells express the growth factor gdf6a.
source: We find that veil cells not only express the growth factor gdf6a but, moreover, this expression distinguishes them from both the adjacent atoh1-positive rhombic lip cells and the majority of squamous roof plate cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data showing gdf6a expression in veil cells.

claim: In transverse section, gdf6a is strongly expressed in a single cell thick domain that precisely abuts the expression domain of atoh1 in the columnar rhombic lip.
source: In transverse section, gdf6a is seen to be strongly expressed in a single cell thick domain that precisely abuts the expression domain of atoh1 in the columnar rhombic lip (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridization data showing spatial relationship of gdf6a and atoh1 expression.

claim: Veil cells comprise a single cell wide signalling centre that organises the adjacent rhombic lip.
source: This suggests that veil cells comprise a single cell wide signalling centre that organises the adjacent rhombic lip.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the expression pattern of gdf6a in veil cells and their spatial relationship to the rhombic lip.

claim: Some veil cells can directly transform into squamous roof plate cells by progressive retraction of their veil over 2 to 3 hours.
source: We find some veil cells can directly transform into squamous roof plate cells in a similar manner to the pioneering dorsal cells that initiate roof plate expansion. Veil cells are able detach gradually from the columnar rhombic lip by a slow, progressive retraction of their veil (2 to 3 hr) and intercalate directly into the roof plate (n = 33, Figure 5A; Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing veil cell transformation.

claim: Direct transformation of veil cells into squamous roof plate cells occurs predominantly in the lower rhombic lip.
source: The direct transformation of veil cells into squamous roof plate cells occurs predominantly in the lower rhombic lip (Figure 5B) and, by implication from in situ labelling, is accompanied by the downregulation of Gdf6a.
evidence: This claim is supported by mapping data showing the spatial distribution of transformation events.

claim: Squamous roof plate cells were not observed to transform back into veil cells.
source: Importantly, we did not see any squamous roof plate cells transform back into veil cells, nor neuroepithelial cells transforming into veil cells in over 1000 hr of recorded development.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative observations from extensive time-lapse imaging.

claim: Neuroepithelial cells were not observed transforming into veil cells in over 1000 hours of recorded development.
source: Importantly, we did not see any squamous roof plate cells transform back into veil cells, nor neuroepithelial cells transforming into veil cells in over 1000 hr of recorded development.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative observations from extensive time-lapse imaging.

claim: Only 11 cell divisions were observed within the squamous epithelium itself over approximately 1100 hours recorded at 24-36 hpf.
source: By contrast, we only observed 11 cell divisions within the squamous epithelium itself over the course of 124 time-lapse recordings (approximately 1100 hr recorded at 24–36 hpf), suggesting that such mitoses are extremely rare.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell division events from time-lapse imaging.

claim: Veil cells are capable of both self-renewing asymmetric divisions and symmetrically fated divisions.
source: Analyses of the daughters of these divisions revealed veil cells are capable of both self-renewing asymmetric divisions and symmetrically fated divisions.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data tracking cell division outcomes.

claim: Veil cell mitosis is preceded by a remodelling of the cell's lateral veil, which undergoes cytoplasmic retraction leaving spikey, skeletal adhesions at the periphery.
source: Time-lapse analysis shows that veil cell mitosis is preceded by a remodelling of the cell's lateral veil, which undergoes a cytoplasmic retraction leaving spikey, skeletal adhesions at the periphery of the veil (n = 27, Figure 6B; Figure 6—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing pre-mitotic veil remodeling.

claim: There is no interkinetic nuclear migration accompanying the veil cell cycle.
source: However, unlike their neighbouring columnar neuroepithelial cells, there is no interkinetic nuclear migration accompnying the veil cell cycle.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing nuclear behavior during veil cell division.

claim: In asymmetrically fated divisions, one daughter differentiates into a squamous roof plate cell while the more lateral daughter remains in the transition zone to replenish the veil cell population.
source: In asymmetrically fated divisions (Figure 6—video 2, n = 26), while one daughter differentiates into a squamous roof plate cell, the more lateral daughter remains in the transition zone to replenish the veil cell population (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data tracking daughter cell fates after asymmetric division.

claim: Asymmetrically fated divisions are predominantly distributed along the lower rhombic lip.
source: These asymmetrically fated divisions are predominantly distributed along the lower rhombic lip (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by mapping data showing the spatial distribution of asymmetric divisions.

claim: In symmetric divisions, one daughter cell generally inherits the veil while the other daughter generates a new lateral veil extension after mitosis.
source: During symmetric divisions, one daughter cell generally inherits the veil, while the other daughter generates a new lateral veil extension after mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing veil inheritance patterns in symmetric divisions.

claim: Symmetrically fated cell divisions are more frequently found along the upper rhombic lip.
source: Symmetrically fated cell divisions are more frequently found along the upper rhombic lip (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by mapping data showing the spatial distribution of symmetric divisions.

claim: Veil cell divisions never produce daughters that populate the columnar epithelium of the rhombic lip.
source: Veil cell divisions never produce daughters that populate the columnar epithelium of the rhombic lip, thus through symmetric and asymmetric divisions they behave as a unipotent stem zone for the squamous roof plate.
evidence: This claim is supported by negative observations from time-lapse imaging and represents a conclusion about veil cell potency.

claim: Veil cells behave as a unipotent stem zone for the squamous roof plate through symmetric and asymmetric divisions.
source: Veil cell divisions never produce daughters that populate the columnar epithelium of the rhombic lip, thus through symmetric and asymmetric divisions they behave as a unipotent stem zone for the squamous roof plate.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from observations of veil cell division patterns and daughter cell fates.

claim: Recoil speeds are significantly higher across the mediolateral axis of the roof plate compared to other axes.
source: This mapping revealed significantly higher recoil speeds across the mediolateral axis of the roof plate compared to recoil speeds along other axes of the epithelium.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of laser ablation experiments measuring tissue tension.

claim: In rare cases of symmetrically fated veil cell divisions where the daughter cell that generates a new veil positions its veil directly over the veil of its sister cell, the second veil fails to establish contact with the rhombic lip and this daughter cell undergoes extrusion and subsequent cell death.
source: In a small number of cases (n = 3) of symmetrically fated veil cell divisions, the daughter cell that generates a new veil positions its veil directly over the veil of its sister cell. In these cases, the second veil fails to establish contact with the rhombic lip and this daughter cell undergoes extrusion from the epithelium and subsequent cell death (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by time-lapse imaging data showing cell extrusion events.

claim: Krox20-driven expression of a dominant negative version of Rab11a (Rabl11a-S25N) in rhombomeres 3 and 5 inhibits ventricle formation in these segments.
source: Krox20-driven expression of a dominant negative version of Rab11a (Rabl11a-S25N) in rhombomeres 3 and 5 inhibits ventricle formation in these segments (Buckley et al., 2013) and non-autonomously restricts expansion of the ventricles in adjacent segments, particularly rhombomere 4 (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to previous work (Buckley et al., 2013).

claim: 38% of asymmetrically fated divisions are followed by extrusion in mini roof plates versus only 5% in wild-type roof plates.
source: We quantified extrusion as a proportion of overall asymmetric divisions and found that 38% of asymmetrically fated divisions are followed by extrusion in the mini roof plates (n = 5/13 divisions) versus only 5% in wild-type roof plates (n = 1/21 divisions) (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell extrusion events in experimental and control conditions.

claim: Physical restriction of roof plate expansion may not limit the number of veil cell mitoses but does control the fate of their daughters in a manner that suggests veil cell fate is regulated by the space available for roof plate growth.
source: This suggests physical restriction of roof plate expansion may not limit the number of veil cell mitoses but does control the fate of their daughters in a manner that suggests veil cell fate is regulated by the space available for roof plate growth.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion inferred from experimental data showing differential extrusion rates under space-restricted conditions.

claim: Squamous cells are 10 times more frequently extruded in mini roof plates than in rhombomere four territory in controls.
source: When instances of cell extrusion are logged in time-lapse recordings of mini roof plates (Figure 7F, right), squamous cells are 10 times more frequently extruded (a total of 17 extrusions in 3560 min of imaging, that is 1 extrusion every 200 min) than in rhombomere four territory in controls (5 extrusions in 9635 min or 0.1 extrusions every 200 min).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of cell extrusion frequency in experimental versus control conditions.

claim: The survival of veil cell daughters depends on available space both within the veil cell domain itself and within the squamous epithelium.
source: Taken together these data suggest the survival of veil cell daughters depends on available space both within the veil cell domain itself and within the squamous epithelium.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from experimental data showing space-dependent cell extrusion.

claim: Extrusion may represent an adaptive mechanism that is able to regionally regulate the number of squamous roof plate cells according to the area of the roof plate itself.
source: Thus, extrusion may represent an adaptive mechanism that is able to regionally regulate the number of squamous roof plate cells according to the area of the roof plate itself.
evidence: This claim is a speculative conclusion drawn from observations of cell extrusion patterns.

claim: The rhombic lip is the progenitor pool for glutamatergic neurons of the cerebellum.
source: In the hindbrain, this epithelial transition is located adjacent to the rhombic lip, which is the progenitor pool for glutamatergic neurons of the cerebellum (Machold and Fishell, 2005; Wang et al., 2005) and hindbrain pre-cerebellar, auditory and vestibular systems (Wang et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Machold and Fishell, 2005; Wang et al., 2005).

claim: Rhombic lip progenitors are specified by the bHLH transcription factor atoh1.
source: Rhombic lip progenitors are part of the columnar neuroepithelium and are specified by the bHLH transcription factor atoh1 (Ben-Arie et al., 1997), which is induced (Alder et al., 1999; Lee et al., 2000) and maintained by Gdf secreted from the periphery of the adjacent roof plate (Broom et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Ben-Arie et al., 1997).

claim: atoh1 is induced by Gdf secreted from the periphery of the adjacent roof plate.
source: Rhombic lip progenitors are part of the columnar neuroepithelium and are specified by the bHLH transcription factor atoh1 (Ben-Arie et al., 1997), which is induced (Alder et al., 1999; Lee et al., 2000) and maintained by Gdf secreted from the periphery of the adjacent roof plate (Broom et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Alder et al., 1999; Lee et al., 2000).

claim: atoh1 is maintained by Gdf secreted from the periphery of the adjacent roof plate.
source: Rhombic lip progenitors are part of the columnar neuroepithelium and are specified by the bHLH transcription factor atoh1 (Ben-Arie et al., 1997), which is induced (Alder et al., 1999; Lee et al., 2000) and maintained by Gdf secreted from the periphery of the adjacent roof plate (Broom et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Broom et al., 2012).

claim: gdf-expressing cells give rise to the simple squamous epithelium of the roof plate.
source: While atoh1-positive precursors at the rhombic lip give rise to populations of neurons, the adjacent gdf-expressing cells give rise to the simple squamous epithelium of the roof plate (Currle et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Currle et al., 2005).

claim: The signaling and progenitor pool complex is maintained by cell-cell interactions mediated by Delta-Notch signaling at the interface between the roof plate and the neuroepithelium.
source: This signaling and progenitor pool complex is maintained by cell-cell interactions (mediated by Delta-Notch signaling) at the interface between the roof plate and the neuroepithelium (Broom et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Broom et al., 2012).

claim: Epithelial transition zones are important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the retina.
source: While conspicuously under-explored, various lines of evidence point to epithelial transition zones as stem cell niches (Mcnairn and Guasch, 2011) and as important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the retina (McKelvie et al., 2002), lower gut (Grodsky, 1961) and cervix (Fluhmann, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (McKelvie et al., 2002).

claim: Epithelial transition zones are important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the lower gut.
source: While conspicuously under-explored, various lines of evidence point to epithelial transition zones as stem cell niches (Mcnairn and Guasch, 2011) and as important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the retina (McKelvie et al., 2002), lower gut (Grodsky, 1961) and cervix (Fluhmann, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Grodsky, 1961).

claim: Epithelial transition zones are important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the cervix.
source: While conspicuously under-explored, various lines of evidence point to epithelial transition zones as stem cell niches (Mcnairn and Guasch, 2011) and as important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the retina (McKelvie et al., 2002), lower gut (Grodsky, 1961) and cervix (Fluhmann, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Fluhmann, 1960).

claim: Various lines of evidence point to epithelial transition zones as stem cell niches.
source: While conspicuously under-explored, various lines of evidence point to epithelial transition zones as stem cell niches (Mcnairn and Guasch, 2011) and as important sites of cells of origin of cancer in the retina (McKelvie et al., 2002), lower gut (Grodsky, 1961) and cervix (Fluhmann, 1960).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Mcnairn and Guasch, 2011).

claim: The majority of the ventricular roof plate in mammals is derived from a Gdf lineage.
source: The majority of the ventricular roof plate in mammals derived from a Gdf lineage (Currle et al., 2005) and our work in the fish gives, for the first time, a cellular and behavioural identity to these cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work (Currle et al., 2005).

claim: 17% of medulloblastomas can be attributed to cells of origin at the rhombic lip epithelial transition zone.
source: Accordingly, 17% of medulloblastomas (the predominant cancer of hindbrain and cerebellum) can be attributed to cells of origin at the rhombic lip epithelial transition zone (Gibson et al., 2010; Kool et al., 2012): almost as significant as the 25% of cancers that arise in granule cell derivatives of the upper rhombic lip.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Gibson et al., 2010; Kool et al., 2012).

claim: 25% of medulloblastomas arise in granule cell derivatives of the upper rhombic lip.
source: Accordingly, 17% of medulloblastomas (the predominant cancer of hindbrain and cerebellum) can be attributed to cells of origin at the rhombic lip epithelial transition zone (Gibson et al., 2010; Kool et al., 2012): almost as significant as the 25% of cancers that arise in granule cell derivatives of the upper rhombic lip.
evidence: This claim is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Unregulated proliferation in granule cell-derived medulloblastomas can be attributed to a disruption of transit amplification regulation.
source: For the latter, unregulated proliferation can be attributed to a disruption of transit amplification regulation (Goodrich et al., 1997; Wallace and Raff, 1999; Wechsler-Reya and Scott, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Goodrich et al., 1997; Wallace and Raff, 1999; Wechsler-Reya and Scott, 1999).

claim: The early mesenchymal nature and position of pioneer cells above the dorsal midline of the neural tube suggest they share some characteristics with neural crest cells.
source: The early mesenchymal nature and position of these pioneers above the dorsal midline of the neural tube suggest they share some characteristics with neural crest cells.
evidence: This claim is a speculative inference based on the observed characteristics of pioneer cells.

claim: Gdf6a-positive veil cells may act as a classic boundary organizer that regulates growth of both neighbouring columnar neuroepithelial cells and the squamous roof plate.
source: On the assumption of a conservation of function across species, Gdf6a-positive veil cells may also act as a classic boundary organizer that regulates growth of both neighbouring columnar neuroepithelial cells and the squamous roof plate (Broom et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is a speculative inference based on known functions of Gdf signaling and a citation to previous work (Broom et al., 2012).

claim: The dependence of squamous roof plate on a Gdf6a lineage is reminiscent of the requirement for other TGFβ superfamily members in the development of squamous cells in the epithelium of the Drosophila egg chamber.
source: The dependence of squamous roof plate on a Gdf6a lineage is reminiscent of the requirement for other TGFβ superfamily members in the development of squamous cells in the epithelium of the Drosophila egg chamber (Brigaud et al., 2015; Duhart et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim draws a comparison to other systems and is supported by citations to previous work (Brigaud et al., 2015; Duhart et al., 2017).

claim: The orientation of local tensile forces could potentially regulate spindle orientation during veil cell mitoses.
source: The orientation of local tensile forces could potentially regulate spindle orientation during veil cell mitoses (di Pietro et al., 2016; Fink et al., 2011; Nestor-Bergmann et al., 2014) and this could regulate symmetry or asymmetry of daughter cell fate.
evidence: This claim is a speculative hypothesis supported by citations to previous work on mechanical regulation of cell division (di Pietro et al., 2016; Fink et al., 2011; Nestor-Bergmann et al., 2014).

claim: Failure to contain over-proliferation through extrusion or effectively translate stretch into coordinated cell division might lead to deregulated cell division.
source: We speculate the unique architecture and dynamic behaviour of veil cells might be envisaged as a potential 'risk' in development. Failure to contain over-proliferation through extrusion or effectively translate stretch into coordinated cell division might lead to deregulated cell division.
evidence: This claim is explicitly speculative reasoning about potential mechanisms of tumor formation.

claim: Tumour formation in rhombic lip transition zone-derived medulloblastomas may be triggered by a failure to respond correctly to mechanical cues for proliferation control.
source: For the former, tumour formation may be triggered by a failure to respond correctly to mechanical cues for proliferation control.
evidence: This claim is explicitly speculative reasoning about potential mechanisms of tumor formation.

claim: This work introduces a new vertebrate model of epithelial morphogenesis.
source: In summary, our work introduces a new vertebrate model of epithelial morphogenesis and uncovers a novel neural progenitor – the veil cell.
evidence: This claim is a summary statement about the contribution of the work.

claim: This work shows for the first time the de novo generation of a squamous epithelium in vivo.
source: We show for the first time, the de novo generation of a squamous epithelium in vivo, the developmental origin of an epithelial transition zone cell type and characterize its modes of cell division.
evidence: This claim is a summary statement about the novelty of the findings.

claim: This work shows for the first time the developmental origin of an epithelial transition zone cell type.
source: We show for the first time, the de novo generation of a squamous epithelium in vivo, the developmental origin of an epithelial transition zone cell type and characterize its modes of cell division.
evidence: This claim is a summary statement about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Veil cell dynamic properties are adapted to integrate morphogenesis of the squamous roof plate with the growth and morphogenesis of its surrounding columnar neuroepithelium.
source: We show that its dynamic properties are adapted to integrate morphogenesis of the squamous roof plate with the growth and morphogenesis of its surrounding columnar neuroepithelium.
evidence: This claim is a conclusion drawn from observations of veil cell behavior and division patterns.
